paragraphs.text: Mobile adaptation for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — phone layout, overlay sidebar drawer, bottom na
vigation and a manual Desktop/Mobile switch. Standard DSH client plugin.
# dsh-client-ui-mobile
中文 · [](https://github.com/MARYCOMPLEX/dsh-client-ui-mobile/actions/workflows/test.yml)
Mobile adaptation for the DeepSeek Harness **Web GUI**, packaged as a standard DSH client plugin.
The Web shell is desktop-first: a three-column frame with drag handles, hover affordances and 8px re
size targets. On a phone it technically renders, but the conversation is squeezed next to a 56px rai
l and the composer fights the on-screen keyboard. This plugin turns the same URL into a usable phone
interface — no fork, no patch to the shell, no build step.
> Community plugin, not affiliated with DeepSeek. Built and tested against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.2.1
nity plugin, not affiliated with DeepSeek. Built and tested against `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.2.1-rc.2`.
## What it does
Everything below applies at **≤ 768px viewport width**; wider viewports are left untouched.
| Area | Behaviour |

| Frame | Three columns collapse to one; the centre gets the full width |
| Sidebar | Becomes an ove
rlay drawer (`min(86vw, 300px)`) with a dimmed backdrop; tapping a session, a panel or the backdrop

closes it |
| Bottom bar | 56px navigation: **Chat / Sessions / Plugins** (hidden when the Plugins p

anel is not registered) **/ Desktop** |
| Desktop handles | The 8px `col-resize` handles are hidden

— they are not touch targets |
| Right panel | Forced full-screen instead of a docked column |
| Com
poser | 16px inputs so iOS does not zoom on focus; the frame shrinks by the on-screen keyboard heigh

t via `visualViewport` |
| Layout | `100dvh` heights, `env(safe-area-inset-*)` padding for notches a

nd gesture bars |
| Wide content | `pre` and `table` scroll inside their own box instead of widening

the page |
| Settings | The settings modal becomes a full-screen sheet; its 188px side nav turns in
to a horizontal, scrollable tab strip |

### As a bundle (recommended)

Then open **Settings → Plugins** and enable the `mobile-ui` bundle. Enabling a bundle appends its pa
tch layer, which inserts the loader row for you.

If your profile runs with configuration HMR disabled, restart `dsh web` afterwards.
### As a plain row
If you would rather not adopt the bundle, install the package and add the row yourself:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Either way the package must be installed in the profile (`dsh plugin --profile <name> add …`) so the
loader can resolve `dsh-client-ui-mobile` from the profile's `node_modules`.
## The switch
The adaptive layout is **on by default** and can be turned off without uninstalling anything:
- **Desktop** button at the right end of the bar — turns the phone layout off for this browser; the

bar disappears and a small **Mobile** pill stays in the bottom-right corner to turn it back on.
- Th

e choice is stored in `localStorage` under `dsh-client-ui-mobile.enabled` (`"1"` / `"0"`).
- URL esc
ape hatch: `?dshm=off` and `?dshm=on` force the state and remember it. Use this if the adaptive layo

ut itself ever makes a page hard to operate.
- Disabling the whole plugin — **Settings → Plugins**,
or remove the loader row — leaves the GUI exactly as shipped.
## How it works
A DSH client plugin runs in the same browser runtime as the shell, so it can extend the interface th
rough documented seams only:
1. **Global stylesheet** — `ctx.effect` appends a `<style>` element to `document.head` and removes i
t on unload, the same mechanism `dsh-client-ui-theme` uses. Every rule is inside a media query and s

coped to the frame the plugin tags, so the desktop layout is never affected by a partial mount.
2. *
*`shell.bottom` slot** — the bar and the pill are ordinary React components registered into the fram

e's bottom row, so the bar participates in the frame's own grid instead of overlaying content.
3. **
`ctx.layout`** — the bar reads `panelInfo` to highlight the active panel and calls `toggleSidebar()`

/ `selectPanel()` for navigation.
4. **DOM tagging, not class names** — the plugin marks the frame
and its three columns with `data-dshm-*` attributes, because the shell's CSS-module class names are
hashed per build (`pI_x6G_frame`).
### Maintainer note: the grid trap
The drawer leaves normal flow (`position: fixed`). A CSS grid skips out-of-flow items during auto-pl
acement, so without explicit pins the centre column slides into the first track — which is `0px` wid
e — and the whole conversation disappears. The plugin pins all three columns:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The smoke test asserts this, so a future refactor cannot silently reintroduce a black screen.
## Compatibility and limitations
- Targets DSH `0.2.x`. The shell's breakpoints, slot names and `ctx.layout` surface are stable withi

n a minor line, but a new release can still move things underneath.
- No hashed class names are used
; hooks are `data-shell-bottom`, `data-sidebar-collapsed`, `data-rightbar-col`, `data-sidebar-right-

open`, plus the `_handle` class suffix.
- 768px is the plugin's own breakpoint. The shell's right-pa
nel auto-fullscreen switches at `< 768`, so the plugin adds a CSS full-screen fallback for the exact

boundary.
- A plugin can change styles, slots and layout state — it cannot change component interna

ls. Composer behaviour (Enter to send, native gestures) stays whatever the shell ships.
- Tested on
Android Chrome. iOS Safari support (safe areas, visual-viewport keyboard inset) is implemented but n
ot verified on a physical device; reports welcome.
## Development
No build step and no dependencies — `lib/client.js` is the shipped browser bundle, written against t
he `window.__ModuleLoader__` contract.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The smoke test stubs React, the DOM and the cordis context, then asserts: module registration, style
sheet injection, `shell.bottom` registration, button set and copy, and the column pinning described
injection, `shell.bottom` registration, button set and copy, and the column pinning described above.
